hints: Since $AB = AC = \sqrt{80} = 4\sqrt{5}$, $ABC$ is isosceles with base $BC$. Midpoint $M = \left(\dfrac{5 + 1}{2}, \dfrac{6 - 6}{2}\right) = (3, 0)$.
walkthrough:
The altitude of an isosceles triangle bisects its base.
Calculate squared side lengths $AB^2$ and $AC^2$:
$$AB^2 = (5 - (-3))^2 + (6 - 2)^2 = 8^2 + 4^2 = 64 + 16 = 80$$
$$AC^2 = (1 - (-3))^2 + (-6 - 2)^2 = 4^2 + (-8)^2 = 16 + 64 = 80$$

Since $AB = AC = \sqrt{80} = 4\sqrt{5}$, triangle $ABC$ is isosceles. Find the midpoint $M$ of base $BC$:
$$M = \left(\dfrac{5 + 1}{2}, \dfrac{6 + (-6)}{2}\right) = (3, 0)$$

The altitude of an isosceles triangle bisects its base.
Calculate the length of the altitude $AM$ from $A(-3, 2)$ to $M(3, 0)$:
$$AM = \sqrt{(3 - (-3))^2 + (0 - 2)^2} = \sqrt{6^2 + (-2)^2} = \sqrt{36 + 4} = \sqrt{40} = 2\sqrt{10}$$

Calculate the base length $BC$ and the area of triangle $ABC$:
$$BC = \sqrt{(1 - 5)^2 + (-6 - 6)^2} = \sqrt{(-4)^2 + (-12)^2} = \sqrt{16 + 144} = \sqrt{160} = 4\sqrt{10}$$
$$\text{Area} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times BC \times AM = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 4\sqrt{10} \times 2\sqrt{10} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 8 \times 10 = 40$$
